note: Nomination-day report for the fourteen single-member divisions of Newry No. 1 (County Down) rural district. Six Unionist candidates were returned unopposed; no nominations were received for the eight Nationalist divisions (Ballyholland, Carrickcrossan, Clonallon, Clonduff, Drumgath, Glen, Hilltown and Mayo; Newry Telegraph, 15 May 1924, p. 3). There were no retiring members to be deemed re-elected: until the election the district was run by a Commissioner, Major George Howard Brush (Newry Reporter, 29 May 1924, p. 6). Under the 1924 Election Order such seats were casual vacancies for the council to fill. At its first meeting (Tuesday 10 June 1924) the council co-opted three additional councillors (Wm. McCombe, F. J. Clemo and John Kidd Porter), not tied to any division, after two Nationalists invited to stand had declined (Newry Reporter, 12 June 1924, p. 6); the filling of the eight divisions is not traced. These are co-options, not elections (round2-down, 7 Nov 2026). Sole nomination; returned unopposed. Returned unopposed.
